cells: Oversees vigilance administration in central government organizations
Exercises superintendence over CBI in corruption investigations

blocks.content: The Central Vigilance Commission is the main agency for preventing corruption in the Central government.

rows: Non-Statutory Body (derives powers from DSPE Act, 1946)
Premier investigating agency for corruption and major crimes
Supervises vigilance administration in Central Govt & PSUs
Investigates offences referred by Central Govt, Courts, or States

items: CVC is NOT an investigating agency itself; it causes inquiries to be conducted through the CBI or chief vigilance officers of government organisations.
Originally set up as an executive body in 1964, CVC gained statutory status in 2003 following a parliamentary act.
CVC exercises superintendence over CBI's investigation of corruption cases involving Central Government officers.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) was established in 1964 by an executive resolution based on the Santhanam Committee recommendations.
CVC was conferred multi-member statutory status through the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003.
It exercises superintendence over the functioning of the Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE/CBI) regarding offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
The CVC possesses all the powers of a civil court while conducting any inquiry.
It reviews the progress of pending applications for sanction of prosecution under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
